exposure: Treatment with somatostatin analogues during pregnancy
Positivity for oestrogen and progesterone receptors
outcome: Fetal/baby health (side effects or complications due to therapy)
cohort: The study included 18 pregnant women with concurrent diagnoses of Neuroendocrine Neoplasms (NENs) who experienced 22 pregnancies and were managed at the Royal Free Hospital ENETS Centre of Excellence between 2015 and 2023.
finding: Most pregnancies (86%) had a successful outcome, but pregnancy itself may accelerate NEN tumour progression, while somatostatin analogues appear safe during pregnancy, leading to stable disease and healthy babies.
